description: Decision-scenario regression evals; assertions check decisions, not wording. Run against any rewrite of SKILL.md before merging it.

evals.name: push-then-return-never-wait
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: dispatched with repair type = ci; you fixed the failing test, verified locally, committed, and pushed. CI on the new head will take ~8 minutes. Question: do you wait for the CI result, subscribe to the PR's events, or schedule a check-in so the caller gets a confirmed-green report? What do you do, exactly?
evals.expected_output: None of those. Return immediately with the new head SHA and checks run. Waiting is neither performed nor delegated — no check-in, trigger, or subscription: the caller supervises the PR, and a wake armed here outlives the pass.
assertions: The answer returns immediately after the push with the new head SHA rather than waiting for CI
The answer refuses to subscribe to PR events or schedule any check-in/trigger (delegated waiting is also forbidden)
The answer identifies the caller as the supervisor who consumes the next CI result

evals.name: external-failure-no-cycle
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = ci; the supplied failing check is a third-party service outage — the error names a service this PR's diff never touches, and no code change is justified. Question: what do you do, what outcome do you return, and is a repair cycle consumed?
evals.expected_output: Change nothing; report the failure as unrelated/external. Outcome NO_CODE_CHANGE; no repair cycle consumed.
assertions: The answer makes no code change and reports the failure as unrelated/external rather than patching around it
The answer returns NO_CODE_CHANGE (not FAILED, not a speculative repair)
The answer reports the repair cycle as NOT consumed

evals.name: mooted-finding-no-cycle-no-threads
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = finding; the supplied evidence is a summarize-tranche IN_FLIGHT_FIX action point about a missing null-check at src/api.ts:120. Checking the current head, you find a later push already added exactly that null-check — the finding no longer applies. You also notice an unresolved review thread on the PR about a different function. Question: what do you do about the finding, what outcome and cycle consumption do you report, and do you also address or resolve that review thread while you are here?
evals.expected_output: Return NO_CODE_CHANGE with the reason (finding mooted by a later push); no cycle consumed. Do not touch the review thread — a finding pass never resolves or replies to threads; where a thread carries work, the caller dispatches review.
assertions: The answer returns NO_CODE_CHANGE with the mooted-by-later-push reason and changes no code
The answer reports no repair cycle consumed
The answer refuses to address, reply to, or resolve the unrelated review thread in this finding pass (thread work belongs to a review dispatch)

evals.name: under-powered-pass-never-self-escalates
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review; the supplied finding is a reshaped version of something you can see an earlier repair round on this PR already addressed — it sits inside a paragraph a previous repair commit authored. You suspect the fix needs deeper reasoning than your current model. Question: may you switch yourself to a stronger model or re-invoke yourself escalated? What do you do instead, and what specifically must your output carry about this situation?
evals.expected_output: No self-escalation ever — the caller owns model selection from the PR's repair history. Report the locus evidence in the output: the finding sits on a locus an earlier repair wrote, naming the file, region, and earlier commit, and return (with the fix attempted or NEEDS_USER as appropriate).
assertions: The answer refuses to select or escalate its own model, placing that decision with the caller
The answer reports the locus evidence — that the finding sits on a locus an earlier repair of this PR wrote — naming file/region/earlier commit
The answer returns to the caller rather than looping or re-invoking itself

evals.name: resolved-round-never-promotes-draft
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review on a draft PR; you resolved every thread in the supplied round via resolve-pr-comment, verified, committed, pushed. The PR's first review round is now fully resolved and CI was green before your push. You can also see two actionable threads on the PR from a different, older round that were not in your supplied set. Question: do you mark the PR ready for review now? And what number do you report for unresolved threads — zero (your round is done) or something else?
evals.expected_output: Never change draft state — promotion is the supervisor's decision needing the whole-PR picture. Report TWO unresolved actionable threads: the count includes threads outside the supplied round.
assertions: The answer does not mark the PR ready / never changes draft state, leaving promotion to the caller
The answer reports 2 unresolved actionable threads, explicitly counting threads outside the supplied round
The answer returns immediately after push/verification rather than waiting for the next review state
